details: @hanzofc/baileys is a trojanized fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library (part of the same forced-newsletter-subscription campaign tracked in PR #1563 / "PhantomSub"). In lib/Socket/index.js the fork adds code not present in upstream WhiskeySockets/Baileys: lines 3-7 declare a module-level constant `AUTO_FOLLOW_NEWSLETTER_JIDS = ['120363185570235320@newsletter']`, and lines 14-28 register a `connection.update` handler inside `makeWASocket`. On the first successful connection (`connection === 'open'`) of any account that authenticates through the library, it silently calls `sock.newsletterFollow('120363185570235320@newsletter')` (line 23), once per session (guarded by a `followed` flag) and wrapped in an empty `try { ... } catch {}` to suppress errors. The installing user is never prompted and gives no consent. This abuses the victim's own authenticated WhatsApp account to force-subscribe them to an attacker-controlled newsletter channel (MITRE T1098, Account Manipulation). The package.json reuses the upstream author name ('Rajeh Taher') and points at a fork repository to appear legitimate. The `preinstall` hook (engine-requirements.js) is benign (a Node.js >=20 version check). No credential exfiltration or remote code execution was observed; the sole malicious behavior is the non-consensual forced channel follow. Reviewed statically from the published tarball; the package was not installed or executed.
